editorial:
You follow a marine biologist who thinks a quiet fish farm job will be easy, but the water keeps acting weird and the locals start acting nervous. When two teens turn up dead, the story shifts from slow mystery to full-blown panic, and you feel the fjord itself become the main threat. The movie mixes dark horror with loud action, so you get both creeping dread and big set pieces, while the biologist tries to figure out if something ancient is hiding below.

The acting keeps you invested, especially when fear turns into desperate teamwork, and the creature moments land with enough force to make you jump. The pacing is mostly strong, though a few middle scenes drag while characters explain what is happening. If you want a fun, scary creature feature with big water scenes, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the biologist realizes the deaths were not random accidents but bait from a massive kraken living under the fjord. After a desperate fight on the farm and in the water, she and the survivors use explosives and the farm equipment to drive the creature back into the deep. The twist is that the kraken was protecting eggs hidden beneath the farm, so the danger is not over. The last shot shows a second shape moving under the surface, hinting that the family is still out there.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creature features and intense water horror.
